title: P2 era record (schema v3, as_of/about_year split locked 2026-07-31)
description: One record per era at data/eras/era-N.json. Nine required fields; SCALE and BUYERS carry the money-type split; eras 5-7 add unit_economics. Every quantitative claim is a calibration object. TIME IS TWO FIELDS, NEVER ONE. `as_of` is PROVENANCE: the date the governing source published, filed or was retrieved. `about_year` is the FACT YEAR: the single calendar year the claim is about. They are different questions and they routinely differ by decades (ds-gdp-001 has as_of 2008-09-14 for a 1922 fact). A chart, a timeline, an axis or any time filter reads `about_year` and only `about_year`; `as_of` may appear in a tooltip or provenance panel and must never be placed on an axis. Decision and full audit of all 505 claims: research/notes/asof-audit.md, data/verification/asof-audit.json, data/verification/REPAIR-P1.md.

id.description: e.g. e3-scale-004; unique across ALL eras

as_of.description: PROVENANCE ONLY: when the governing source published, filed or was retrieved. It identifies the VINTAGE of the number, which matters because compilers revise (e4-scale-006 is one 1990 total printed differently in a 2001 and a 2009 edition). It is NOT the year the fact is about, it MUST NOT be read as one, and it must never be placed on a time axis or used as a time filter. Month and day precision is legitimate here and is present on 160 values. A bare year in this field is a coarse vintage, not a fact year.

about_year.description: THE FACT YEAR: the single calendar year the claim is about, and the ONLY field a chart, timeline or time axis may read. Exactly one integer, always. Where the fact genuinely covers a range, `about_year` is the anchor point and `about_span` carries the range; where the anchor was assumed rather than read from evidence, `timeline_ready` is false and the claim may not be drawn at all. This is claims.json getting what adspend.json already has as its `year` field.

about_span.description: OPTIONAL: [start, end] where the fact covers more than one year - a season, a cycle, a growth interval, an era-typical practice. A chart draws the band and anchors the point at `about_year`, which must lie inside the span. Absent means the fact is a single year. Never used to disguise ignorance: a claim whose year is unknown carries timeline_ready false, not a span the width of an era.

timeline_ready.description: OPTIONAL, defaults to TRUE when absent. False means `about_year` was assumed rather than read from evidence, and the claim MUST NOT be drawn on a timeline until a source is read. Seven claims are false: six need a source read, and ds-provenance-001 is about the dataset itself and never belongs on a history axis.

about_year_note.description: REQUIRED in two cases, enforced by tools/verify_p2.py p1-timeline: when `timeline_ready` is false, saying what has to be read; and when `about_year` matches no year appearing in the claim's own statement or unit, saying why the timeline year differs from the text. A timeline year may disagree with the claim's prose, but never silently.

method.description: REQUIRED when grade is C: how the triangulation was built

money_type_split.description: Each key holds a claim, or an absence note where the era genuinely cannot source it.

note.description: Why no credible figure exists and what was tried

summary.description: The field's narrative answer for this era, self-contained

unit_economics.description: REQUIRED for eras 5, 6, 7. Revenue, cost, margin per unit of attention.

comparison_series.description: Era 7 only: the 2023-2026 LLM inference cost-per-query series

boundary_notes.description: Facts shared with neighboring eras, stated so V1 can cross-check agreement
